evidence.source: 國學大全 字形演變
evidence.field: listed historical forms and component analysis
evidence.text: The page lists 忘 on a late Spring-and-Autumn bronze vessel, Warring States inscriptions, and in seal, clerical, and regular scripts; it describes 心 as semantic and 亡 as phonetic from bronze script onward. This is a secondary paleographic account, and its listed examples do not establish the earliest occurrence.
evidence.title: 忘字形演变字源_汉字「忘」

evidence.source: 中國哲學書電子化計劃
evidence.text: Search-result text quotes the Shuowen entry as 不識也。从心从亡，亡亦聲 (“not to recognize/know”; composed of 心 and 亡, with 亡 also phonetic). Opening the page failed, so this quotation was not independently checked on the opened page in this pass.
evidence.title: 忘 - 中國哲學書電子化計劃

evidence.field: glyph origin and competing word-etymology proposal
evidence.text: The entry labels 忘 a 心 + 亡 phonosemantic compound and reports an alternative word-history proposal: that 忘 was originally the same word as 亡 and later took a perfective suffix *-s or *-h, citing Schuessler (2007). This is a tertiary account; it does not by itself establish the proposal or date graph formation.
evidence.title: 忘 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.text: The entry gives 忘 as Middle Chinese mjang and mjangH and Old Chinese *maŋ and *maŋ-s; its Zhengzhang section names 亡 as sound component and gives 忘 *maŋ/*maŋs. The supplied exact local Baxter–Sagart rows agree for 亡 (*maŋ; MC mjang) and 忘 (*maŋ and *maŋ-s; MC mjang and mjangH), from sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv. These reconstructions support a close comparison in the named system, but do not date the compound or establish a specific sound change.
evidence.kind: tertiary reconstruction summary cross-checked against supplied local rows
evidence.title: 忘 - 维基词典，自由的多语言词典

evidence.text: The official U+5FD8 record gives kMandarin wàng and kDefinition “forget; neglect; miss, omit.” The supplied local exact Unihan rows also give 忘 wàng and 亡 wáng in sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt. These are current character metadata, not evidence for an ancient phonetic relationship or for semantic chronology.
evidence.kind: official Unicode record cross-checked against supplied local rows
evidence.title: Unihan data for U+5FD8

evidence.text: The official U+4EA1 record gives kMandarin wáng and kDefinition “death, destroyed; lose, perish.” This is current metadata, not evidence for an ancient sound relationship or for a whole-graph borrowing claim.

search_audit.query: 忘 bronze inscription paleography 心 亡 phonetic Shuowen 忘 earliest form
search_audit.outcome: Search returned the paleographic summary and additional sources. Opened the paleographic summary; it lists late Spring-and-Autumn bronze and later forms, and describes 心 plus phonetic 亡. The other two pages returned internal errors when opened.

search_audit.query: 忘 說文 不識也 詩經 early textual attestation 忘
search_audit.outcome: Search surfaced the Shuowen quotation. Opening CText failed; opened Wiktionary, which supplied a tertiary quotation and an attributed perfective-suffix proposal. No securely dated early textual use was verified.
Direct opens returned internal errors. Then followed the Unihan links from the opened Wiktionary character pages; both official Unicode records opened and showed 忘 wàng and 亡 wáng.

search_audit.query: Baxter Sagart 2014 忘 亡 *maŋ *maŋ-s phonetic component
search_audit.outcome: Opened both character entries. The Chinese entry gives named-system reconstructions for 忘 and identifies 亡 in the Zhengzhang sound-component field; the English entry labels the phonosemantic analysis and the Old Chinese series. Cross-checked the supplied exact local Baxter–Sagart rows for 忘 and 亡.

gaps: No securely dated oracle-bone occurrence or Shang-era attestation of 忘 was verified. The accessible paleographic summary begins its listed 忘 examples with later bronze material; that does not prove the graph first arose then.
No primary inscription image was inspected, so the exact stroke development, individual graphic variants, and any possible corruption remain unassessed.
No dated textual attestations were established to order the glosses ‘forget’, ‘neglect’, ‘miss’, and ‘omit’; do not infer that semantic chronology from the Shuowen gloss or modern Unihan definitions.

The perfective-suffix proposal reported by Wiktionary remains unresolved: this pass did not inspect the cited scholarly argument or establish separate, dated histories of 亡 and 忘 as spoken words. No independent whole-graph borrowing analysis was found.

Modern Mandarin wàng and wáng were verified in Unihan. Similarity of the historical readings is supported by the supplied same-system Baxter–Sagart rows and the cited phonetic analysis; modern readings alone do not establish the ancient relationship.
